sentences.text: Antusuchus possessed a skull measuring about 11.5 cm in length.
Two specimens were recovered together from the Cenomanian Candeleros Formation.
Its blade-like, serrated teeth indicate a carnivorous diet.
The close association of the two individuals has been interpreted as evidence that Antusuchus may have lived in groups.
Antusuchus is placed within the family Peirosauridae.
Phylogenetic studies suggest it occupies the most basal position among peirosaurids.
The fossils date to the Albian stage.
They were found in the Rio Negro Province of Argentina, in northern Patagonia.
The La Buitrera locality, where the remains occur, is interpreted as a wind-influenced dryland fluvial environment.
Researchers debate whether Antusuchus represents a distinct basal lineage or shows intermediate features between peirosaurids and other notosuchians.
